title: The AI-bubble skeptic / short case - who is betting against or warning, and what they cite (the adversarial check)
source: Public record: Michael Burry / Scion Asset Management Q3-2025 13F (filed ~Nov 2025): put options on ~5M Palantir shares (~$912M notional) + ~1M NVIDIA shares (~$187M notional) - together ~80% of the disclosed book; subsequently detailed/expanded (NVIDIA puts $110 strike exp 2027; Palantir puts $100 strike Dec 2026 + $50 strike Jun 2027 plus direct short; added shorts on Oracle, the SOXX semis ETF, and QQQ). Burry publicly accused AI hyperscalers of understating depreciation by extending the useful life of compute equipment on a 2-3yr product cycle - 'one of the more common frauds of the modern era' - and drew a dot-com-fiber-overbuild parallel (CNBC, Sherwood, Bloomberg, Nov 2025). David Cahn (Sequoia) 'AI's $600B Question' (Jun 2024, updated from the Sept 2023 '$200B Question'): working backward from NVIDIA run-rate revenue x2 (GPUs ~half of datacenter TCO) x2 (50% end-user gross margin) to the revenue needed to justify the capex; by 2026 the implied annual gap is ~$800B+, with Allianz pegging the capex-vs-revenue divergence at ~46% vs ~32% in the 2001 telecom bubble. MIT 'GenAI Divide' / Project NANDA (Aug 2025): ~95% of enterprise GenAI pilots delivered zero measurable P&L impact despite ~$30-40B spend; only ~5% created significant value (external tools succeeded ~2x internal builds). HONESTY/GRADE: the 13F disclosure, the Cahn framework, and the MIT study are FACT; whether the skeptics are RIGHT is the OPEN question and is NOT asserted - the honest caveats are recorded: 13F put NOTIONAL is not capital-at-risk and can be a hedge; the positions took immediate paper losses as both stocks kept rising; Burry has a mixed timing record (his 2021 Tesla puts preceded a doubling); Cahn himself explicitly called it a TIME-LAG, NOT a bubble, and stayed long-term bullish; and real enterprise AI consumption is accelerating even as realized ROI stays weak (both true at once). This block is the adversarial/steelman complement to the AI-capex map - structural overlay edges only; the financial proof core is untouched. Burry's depreciation critique maps onto the existing depreciation/duration-mismatch Z3 proof (fin-ai-depreciation-debttrap).

edges.notes: Michael Burry / Scion disclosed put options on ~1M NVIDIA shares (~$187M notional) in the Q3-2025 13F; later detailed as $110-strike puts expiring 2027. Thesis: AI capex is a dot-com-fiber-style overbuild and hyperscalers understate depreciation by extending GPU useful life. FACT: the disclosed position + the stated thesis. CAVEAT (recorded): 13F put notional is not capital-at-risk; the position took immediate paper losses as NVIDIA kept rising; Burry's timing record is mixed. 'Validates' = a documented bearish bet/claim ABOUT the node, not an endorsement that it is correct.

Burry's largest disclosed bet: puts on ~5M Palantir shares (~$912M notional), later a dual-strike structure ($100 Dec 2026 + $50 Jun 2027) plus a direct short - a valuation-multiple critique on a stock up ~176% on the year. Same caveats (notional, paper losses, timing).

Burry added a short on Oracle (plus the SOXX semis ETF and QQQ) - consistent with the Oracle debt-funded-capex / RPO-concentration credit thread (cross-ref spec-oracle-ai-credit-lynchpin). FACT of the disclosed short; correctness not asserted.

Core skeptic argument on the asset side: depreciation/useful-life EXTENSION on 2-3yr-cycle compute artificially boosts earnings (Burry's 'fraud of the modern era' claim), and the MIT 'GenAI Divide' study found ~95% of enterprise GenAI pilots delivered zero measurable P&L impact. Maps onto the existing depreciation/duration-mismatch Z3 proof (fin-ai-depreciation-debttrap). FACT: the critique + the study; INTERPRETATION (labeled): that it proves a bubble.
edges.source: MIT Project NANDA Aug 2025 / Burry Nov 2025

edges.notes: David Cahn (Sequoia) 'AI's $600B Question' is the most-cited capex-vs-revenue frame: the revenue needed to justify the buildout (NVIDIA run-rate x2 x2) has outrun actual AI revenue by an order of magnitude (~$800B+ implied annual gap by 2026). CAVEAT (recorded): Cahn explicitly framed this as a TIME-LAG, not a bubble, and stayed long-term bullish - the gap is a survival-of-the-gap question, not a verdict.

The neocloud pure-plays are the skeptics' sharpest target - CoreWeave's junk-level debt pricing and CDS default-odds are the market already pricing part of the bear case (cross-ref spec-coreweave-credit-stress-2026). FACT of the market signals; the doom-loop read is labeled.

The skeptic case converges with the official-sector warnings (BIS 'shadow borrowing', IMF) and the circular-financing critics: capex funded by debt/insurance credit against a fast-depreciating, revenue-light asset. This is the bear framing of the same structure the robustness certificate and off-balance-sheet ledger measure (cross-ref core_robustness, spec-offbalancesheet-ai-financing). FACT of the convergence; severity = contested.
